title: Isandro and the Oath
premise: Odile Sandoval has spent three years selling harmless charms in Corvessa, a city where the guilds that once kept magic alive have been outlawed and hunted to extinction. When a mute child appears at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Odile discovers the child is a living fragment of the Oath — the broken covenant between the human realm and the hidden world of the Vael — and that its collapse is already bleeding magic and monsters into the city. Pursued by the Crown's witch-hunters and betrayed by the guildmaster who raised her, Odile must gather the last oath-keepers and reforge the covenant at the Sunken Altar, a ritual that demands a life freely given. In the end, Odile refuses both sacrifice and power, instead binding the Oath to the child — now revealed as the heir of both realms — and the covenant is reborn not as a chain of duty but as a promise freely renewed, at the cost of Odile's own magic.
about_author: Ada Halloran is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction, a career that left her obsessed with oaths, seals, and the weight of inherited promises. She writes fantasy from a drafty house on the coast, where she claims the fog does most of the plotting.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A day in Corvessa's night market: Odile sells luck-knots and fever-charms to customers who don't know they're buying outlawed magic, while hunter patrols and the memory of the guild's fall shadow every sale. The beat is quiet defiance — a woman keeping a dead tradition alive one small charm at a time.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Late at night, a child of about nine arrives barefoot at Odile's attic door, speaking a language that makes Odile's charms hum in answer. When Odile replies in the old guild-tongue, the child switches to hers. The beat is wonder curdling into fear as Odile realizes the child was not lost — she was sent.

chapters.title: What the Bells Remember
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile seeks Master Ferren, her guildmaster in hiding, who identifies the language as Oathscript — the tongue in which the covenant between realms was first sworn. The Oath is failing, he says, and the child is a fragment of it made flesh. The beat is dread and reluctant inheritance: Odile wanted to be forgotten by history, not chosen by it.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Smoke
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Witch-hunters raid the night market on a tip and Odile escapes with the child through the city's drowned undercrofts, using magic openly for the first time in three years. A disgraced hunter named Renn sees them — and lets them go. The beat is terror giving way to a first, fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Child Who Speaks in Two Tongues
chapters.summary: The child's POV, close third. She remembers being the Oath itself — a promise with no name — before it was broken and she was cast out. Through her eyes Odile is something new: a keeper who keeps out of love, not law. The beat is alien tenderness and the first hint that the child is more than a messenger.

chapters.title: The Last Guildhouse
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ferren gathers the surviving oath-keepers: a blind cartographer, a defrocked priest, and Renn, who arrives uninvited. They map the route to the Sunken Altar where the Oath was first sworn — and learn the ritual demands a life freely given. The beat is uneasy fellowship forged around a terrible price.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ferren betrays them, selling the child's location to the Crown in exchange for a pardon and the guild's restoration. Odile realizes he taught her everything except how to recognize ambition wearing duty's face. The beat is heartbreak and fury — power's corruption made painfully personal.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Drowned Quarter
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Now openly a traitor to the hunters, Renn leads Odile and the child through the flooded district as the failing Oath warps the city — rivers running backward, stone remembering being bone. The beat is desperate momentum and Renn's dawning conviction that he has finally joined the right side of the law.

chapters.title: The Vael Gate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A standing stone opens into the Vael realm, where Odile meets Seryth, a warden who blames humans for breaking the Oath and wants to let the covenant die so her realm can be sealed forever. The beat is cold confrontation — love against duty, with entire worlds as the stakes.

chapters.title: A Promise With No Name
chapters.summary: The child's POV. In the Vael realm her memory deepens: she was not merely a fragment of the Oath but its heart, and the one who broke it was a keeper who loved someone on the far side of the covenant. The beat is tragic revelation — the last keeper who chose love unmade everything.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map of Ends
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The blind cartographer reveals the Altar is reached only by a road that shows each traveler the ending they fear most. Odile walks it and sees herself alone, magic gone, the child gone, the city indifferent. The beat is confrontation with her deepest fear: that love and duty demand the same terrible coin.

chapters.title: The Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ferren's POV. Restored to his guildhouse, Ferren learns the Crown never meant to pardon anyone — they intend to seize the child and wield the Oath's power as a weapon. His triumph sours into horror. The beat is the corrupter corrupted, as Ferren begins to grasp what he has truly sold.

chapters.title: Seryth's Testimony
chapters.summary: Seryth's POV. Seryth recounts the Oath's breaking three centuries ago and, reluctantly, the deeper truth: the realms were never meant to be separate, and the Vael are dying as surely as human magic. Her duty to seal the gate wars with the evidence before her eyes. The beat is grief cracking ideology.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Standing Stones
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Crown's hunters, guided by Ferren's intelligence and a zealous captain, assault the gate. Renn holds the pass; the cartographer dies buying time. Odile escapes into the Vael realm with the child as the gate collapses behind them. The beat is sacrifice and survival — the fellowship pays its first blood price.

chapters.title: Where the Altar Sleeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Guided by the child's memories, they cross the dying Vael lands to the Sunken Altar, a cathedral of roots and drowned light. Seryth bars the way, and Odile offers not a fight but the truth: sealing the gate kills both worlds. The beat is persuasion as the highest form of courage.

chapters.title: Ferren's Return
chapters.summary: Ferren's POV. Having led the Crown's forces through the ruined gate, Ferren arrives at the Altar to seize the child — and instead kneels, offering his own life for the ritual, too late to undo his betrayal but not too late to pay for it. The beat is ruinous repentance.

chapters.title: The Price of the Oath
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The ritual begins and demands its freely given life. Odile prepares to give her own; the child stops her, revealing that the Oath was broken by sacrifice in the first place — a covenant built on death was always doomed. The beat is the story's thesis spoken aloud: duty that costs love is already broken.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, the child's voice braided in. The Crown's captain breaches the Altar; amid the chaos Odile does the unprecedented — she swears the Oath anew not with a death but with a surrender of her own magic into the child, making the covenant a living heir instead of a dead law. The beat is the climax: love and duty reconciled at last.

chapters.title: Two Realms, One Sky
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The reforged Oath floods both realms: magic returns openly to Corvessa, the Vael lands bloom, and the wall between worlds thins to a veil anyone may cross with permission. The captain, confronted with a miracle his orders never anticipated, lowers his sword. The beat is awe — the world remade in a single dawn.

chapters.title: What Odile Gave Up
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile wakes without her magic — her charms are just knots and thread now — and grieves quietly for the part of herself she surrendered. The child, newly revealed as the Oath's living heir, offers to return it, and Odile refuses. The beat is bittersweet peace: some prices are worth paying twice.

chapters.title: The Guild Reborn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Corvessa rebuilds its guilds on new terms — keepers chosen by the child, bound by promise rather than punishment. Ferren, spared but stripped of rank, asks Odile to teach him what she knows, and Renn retakes the hunter's oath rewritten in Oathscript. The beat is cautious hope and the slow work of building trust worth having.

chapters.title: The Door Stays Open
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A year later, Odile runs a school in her old attic, teaching children the old tongues beside the new. The child — growing, laughing, no longer a fragment but a person — visits through the veil. When a knock comes at the door, Odile opens it without fear. The beat is resolution as beginning: the oath kept, the door open, the story handed on.
